mainTopic: Food bought from non-Jews: fish products and kosher signs, חילתית cut with a knife, trusting a חבר's household, and items left under seal
overview: This amud first finishes a question about wine mixed into food. Wine you can notice in the dish forbids it, and wine you cannot notice does not. Then the גמרא explains the fish products in the משנה. חילק is the small fish סולתנית, which is forbidden only because non-kosher fish come up with it. A fish that grows scales later, or sheds them when caught, is kosher. רבי אבהו and אביי permit fish products whose source is known to be free of non-kosher fish. רבינא later forbids the small fish of the river בב, because other rivers now flow into it. Next come memory aids for which sea creatures are kosher, and stories of חכמים who checked doubtful fish for scales. The גמרא then explains why a sliver of חילתית is forbidden: the sharp spice makes the knife's fat taste good. Stories and ברייתות teach that a חבר's slave and wife are trusted like a חבר, with a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about people who move between households. The amud ends with רב's rule about items left with a non-Jew under one seal, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Wine you can notice versus wine you cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles an earlier contradiction. In one case the wine can be noticed in the food, and in the other case it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, its substance is noticeable. Here, their substance is not noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a contradiction from just before this line, about two rulings on wine mixed into food. It says the two cases are different because the wine can be noticed in one and not in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fish stew ("there"), the wine is a real, noticeable part of the dish, so the food is forbidden. In the pickled vegetables ("here"), the wine cannot be noticed at all, so it does not forbid them. The contradiction goes away because the two cases are not the same.

phrases.english: There, its substance is noticeable,
phrases.notes: "There" is the fish stew with wine in it. "Its substance" means the wine itself.

phrases.english: here, their substance is not noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם יְדִיעַ מַמָּשׁוֹ, הָכָא לָא יְדִיעַ מַמָּשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this part of the daf.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the two wine rulings contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine that can be noticed in the food makes it forbidden. Wine that cannot be noticed does not.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and asking what חילק is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of forbidden fish products and asks what חילק is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: minced טרית fish, and brine with no fish in it, and so on. What is חילק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks what the word חילק means. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists items bought from a non-Jew that are forbidden. These include minced טרית fish, brine with no identifying fish floating in it, and חילק. The גמרא needs to know what חילק is before it can understand the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: a fish product named in the משנה

phrases.english: And minced טרית fish,
and brine that has no fish in it, etc.
What is חילק?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word חילק in the משנה means.

steps.title: רב says חילק is סולתנית
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that חילק is a small fish called סולתנית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר אבא said in the name of רב: this is סולתנית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. חילק is a kind of small fish called סולתנית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סולתנית is a small fish that is usually caught before its scales have grown. That fact raises the next question, which is why it would be forbidden at all.

keyTerms.meaning: a small fish that is usually caught before it grows scales

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Abba said that Rav said:
This is sultanit,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חילק is the small fish סולתנית.

steps.title: Why סולתנית is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that סולתנית is forbidden because non-kosher fish come up mixed with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it forbidden? Because what is mixed in with it comes up together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks why סולתנית is forbidden, and then he answers his own question. Small non-kosher fish get caught along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish itself is not the problem. Because it is so small, other small fish, including non-kosher ones, get mixed in when it is pulled from the water. So the problem is the mixture, not the סולתנית.

keyTerms.meaning: what is mixed in with it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think סולתנית is a non-kosher fish. It is forbidden only because non-kosher fish get caught along with it. The next step shows that the fish itself is kosher.

phrases.english: And for what reason is it forbidden?
Because what is mixed with it comes up with it.
phrases.notes: He means other small, non-kosher fish get pulled out of the water together with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's explanation by giving the reason for the איסור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden because non-kosher fish get mixed in with it, not because the fish itself is non-kosher.

steps.title: Fish that grow scales later or shed them when caught
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a fish that will grow scales later is kosher, and so is a fish that loses its scales when pulled from the sea. סולתנית is one of the examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a fish that has no scales now but will grow them later, such as סולתנית and עפיין, is permitted. A fish that has scales now but will shed them when it comes up from the sea, such as these five kinds, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists סולתנית as a kosher fish. This backs up רב's point that it is forbidden only because of the mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two cases. In the first, a fish has no scales yet but will grow them, and it is kosher. In the second, a fish has scales but drops them when caught, and it is also kosher. Since סולתנית is kosher by itself, the only reason to forbid it is the non-kosher fish caught along with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a lasting rule: a fish counts as having scales even if it has them only at one stage of its life.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If it does not have them now
phrases.notes: "Them" means scales. The ברייתא doesn't say the word, but that's what it's talking about.

phrases.english: but will grow them after some time,
such as the sultanit and the afyan,
phrases.notes: Some versions read עפיץ, in the round brackets. The corrected wording is עפיין, in the square brackets. Either way it is the name of a fish.

phrases.english: it is permitted.
If it has them now
but will shed them
when it comes up from the sea,
such as akunas and afunas,
ketaspatiyas, akhspatiyas, and atunas, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא showing that סולתנית is kosher by itself, which fits רב's reason.
steps.raayaObject: That סולתנית is a kosher fish and is forbidden only because of the mixture.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing fish that grow scales later or shed them when caught.

steps.title: רבי אבהו permits fish innards and eggs from anyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו publicly ruled in קיסרי that fish innards and fish eggs may be bought from anyone, because they are presumed to come from places with no non-kosher fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו announced in קיסרי: fish innards and their eggs may be bought from anyone. The presumption is that they come only from פילוסא and אספמיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו makes a public ruling. Fish innards and fish eggs may be bought even from a non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we would worry that innards or eggs came from non-kosher fish, because once they are taken out you cannot tell which fish they came from. רבי אבהו says these products came only from פילוסא and אספמיא, places where there are no non-kosher fish. So there is nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu announced in Caesarea:
Fish innards and their eggs
may be bought from any person.
Their presumption is that they come
only from Pelusium and Spain,
phrases.notes: The point is that non-kosher fish aren't found in those places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about buying fish products from non-Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish innards and eggs may be bought from anyone, based on a חזקה about where they come from.

steps.title: אביי's similar ruling about small fish from the river of בב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares רבי אבהו's ruling to אביי's ruling that the small fish of the river of בב are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what אביי said: these small fish of the river of בב are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אבהו's ruling follows the same idea as a ruling of אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי permitted small fish from the river of בב without checking each one, since non-kosher fish are not found in that river. Both rulings rely on the same idea. If a place has no non-kosher fish, its fish products may be eaten.
steps.whatToRemember: A fish product can be permitted because of where it comes from. If a place is known to have no non-kosher fish, its fish innards, eggs, or small fish may be bought even from a non-Jew.

phrases.english: Like that which Abaye said:
These small fish of the Bav River are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a matching ruling that rests on the same idea as רבי אבהו's.
steps.raayaObject: That a product may be permitted based on where it comes from.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's ruling about the small fish of the river of בב.

steps.title: Why did אביי permit the fish of בב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling that the small fish of the river of בב are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אביי was not worried about non-kosher fish mixed in with the small fish of בב. This question sets up the next few steps, where the גמרא tries out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 we saw that small fish can be forbidden because non-kosher fish come up mixed with them. So אביי's ruling needs a reason why this river is different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means the reason for אביי's ruling from the last step, that the small fish of the river בב are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling cited in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the small fish of בב are presumed free of non-kosher fish.

steps.title: Fast-flowing water is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that non-kosher fish, which lack a spine, cannot survive in fast water. It rejects this because we see them living there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because the water flows fast, and a non-kosher fish has no spinal cord, so it cannot stay in a place where the water flows fast, that is wrong, because we see that it does stay there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible reason: the river's strong current sweeps away non-kosher fish. Then it immediately rejects that reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that non-kosher fish lack a חוט השדרה, so they are too weak to hold their place in a current. But experience shows non-kosher fish do live in fast rivers, so this cannot be אביי's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)
But we see (what actually happens in real life)

phrases.english: If you say it is because the water flows fast,
and this non-kosher fish,
since it has no spinal cord,
in a place where the water flows fast
it cannot stay,
but we see that it does stay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 8's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: We can see that non-kosher fish do live in fast-flowing water.

steps.title: Salty water is not the reason either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that non-kosher fish, which lack scales, cannot survive in salty water. It rejects this too because we see them there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because the water is salty, and a non-kosher fish has no scales, so it cannot stay in a place where the water is salty. But we see that it does stay there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second reason: the river's water is salty, and non-kosher fish cannot live there. Again, it rejects the reason based on what we see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the weakness is not the spine but the lack of קשקשים (scales), which would supposedly protect a fish from salt. Since non-kosher fish are found in salty water, this reason also fails.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because the water is salty,
and this non-kosher fish,
since it has no scales,
in a place where the water is salty
it cannot stay.
But we see that it does stay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from step 9 with a new one, which is also rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: We can see that non-kosher fish do live in salty water.

steps.title: The mud does not let non-kosher fish breed
steps.stepSummary: The real reason: the mud of the river בב does not allow non-kosher fish to multiply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because the mud there does not let non-kosher fish multiply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final reason for אביי's ruling: the river's mud is not a place where non-kosher fish can breed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the rejected reasons, this one does not claim non-kosher fish can never be in the water. It says they do not reproduce there, so the small fish in that river are presumed to be kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי permitted the small fish of בב because its mud does not let non-kosher fish breed, not because of the current or the salt.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מְרַבֵּה טִינָא דָּג טָמֵא.
phrases.english: Rather, it is because the mud does not let non-kosher fish multiply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מְרַבֵּה טִינָא דָּג טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two rejected reasons, gives the accepted answer to step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mud of the river בב does not let non-kosher fish reproduce.

steps.title: רבינא: nowadays these fish are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that nowadays, since the rivers גוזא and גמדא flow into בב, its small fish are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Nowadays, since the river גוזא and the river גמדא pour into it, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a later update to אביי's ruling: things have changed, so the small fish of בב are now forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's ruling depended on non-kosher fish not breeding in that river. Now other rivers flow into בב and can bring non-kosher fish with them, so the reason no longer protects the small fish.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not arguing with אביי. אביי's reason was right for his time; the situation of the river changed later.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
Nowadays, since there pour into it
the river גוזא and the river גמדא, they are forbidden.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the small fish of the river בב, since non-kosher fish can now come in from these other rivers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits אביי's ruling based on the reason given in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since other rivers now flow into בב, its small fish are forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: the sea donkey is permitted, the sea ox is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the 'sea donkey' is kosher and the 'sea ox' is not, and gives a memory aid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The 'sea donkey' is permitted, the 'sea ox' is forbidden. Your memory aid: impure becomes pure, pure becomes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new ruling about which sea creatures are kosher. אביי names two and gives a way to remember them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On land a donkey is not kosher and an ox is kosher. In the sea the names flip: the 'donkey' is kosher and the 'ox' is not. The memory aid tells you to reverse the land animal's status.

phrases.english: אביי said:
This 'sea donkey' is permitted,
the 'sea ox' is forbidden,
and your memory aid: impure is pure, pure is impure.
phrases.notes: The donkey, not kosher on land, is kosher in the sea; the ox, kosher on land, is not kosher in the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new list of rulings about specific kinds of fish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sea donkey is kosher; the sea ox is not.

steps.title: רב אשי: שפר נונא permitted, קדש נונא forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules on two more fish and ties the forbidden one to the words 'holy to ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: שפר נונא is permitted, קדש נונא is forbidden. Your memory aid: 'holy to ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי continues the list with two more fish names and a memory aid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name קדש sounds like קודש, 'holy'. Something holy belongs to ה׳ and not to people, so you remember that this fish is not for eating.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
שפר נונא is permitted,
קדש נונא is forbidden,
and your memory aid: 'Holy to ה׳.'
phrases.notes: A holy thing belongs to ה׳, not to us, so the 'holy fish' is not for us to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁפַר נוּנָא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling to the list of fish begun by אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שפר נונא is kosher; קדש נונא is not.

steps.title: Another version: קבר נונא is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב אשי's ruling as being about קבר נונא, with the memory aid 'graves of non-Jews'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: קבר נונא is forbidden. Your memory aid: graves of non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רב אשי's ruling, with a different fish name and memory aid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the forbidden fish is called קבר נונא, and קבר means 'grave'. The memory aid links it to graves of non-Jews, reminding you that this fish is not kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: Fish names come with memory aids: sea donkey and שפר נונא are kosher; sea ox and קדש נונא (or קבר נונא) are not.

phrases.english: Some say:
קבר נונא is forbidden,
and your memory aid: graves of non-Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רב אשי's ruling from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, קבר נונא is the forbidden fish.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא finds hidden scales on a strange fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא is shown a fish that looks like a non-kosher creature. He puts it in a basket, sees scales, and permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא came to גינזק. They brought him a fish that looked like a חיפושא, a non-kosher sea creature. He covered it with a basket, saw that it had scales, and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי עקיבא checking a fish that looked non-kosher. He found a way to see its scales and permitted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scales are the sign that makes a fish kosher. The fish looked like a non-kosher type, so its scales were not obvious. Covering it in a basket made it thrash, and its scales came off where he could see them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva happened to come to Ginzak,
they brought before him a certain fish
that looked like a chippusha,
phrases.notes: A חיפושא is a sea creature that isn't kosher, so this fish looked suspicious.

phrases.english: he covered it with a basket,
he saw scales on it, and permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rulings on specific fish, the גמרא moves to stories of חכמים checking doubtful fish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fish that looks like a non-kosher type is permitted if a careful check shows it has scales.

steps.title: רב אשי holds an eel-like fish up to the light
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי is shown a fish that looks like an eel. He holds it up to the daylight, sees tiny scales, and permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי came to טמדוריא. They brought him a fish that looked like an eel. He held it up to the daylight, saw thin scales on it, and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second story of the same kind. רב אשי uses daylight to find tiny scales on a fish that looked like an eel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eels seem to have no scales, so a fish like this looks forbidden. Holding it against the light showed very thin scales, which were enough to permit it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi happened to come to Tamduria,
they brought before him a certain fish
that looked like an eel,
he held it up facing the daylight,
he saw that it had thin scales, and permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story: another חכם uses a different method to find scales.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even very thin scales, seen only against the light, make the fish kosher.

steps.title: רב אשי uses a white vessel to spot scales
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי puts a fish that looks like a שפרנונא into a white vessel, sees the scales against the white, and permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי came to a certain place. They brought him a fish that looked like a שפרנונא. He covered it with white vessels, saw scales, and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third story of checking a doubtful fish. This time רב אשי uses a white container so dark scales would stand out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each story uses a new practical trick to reveal scales: a basket, daylight, and here a white background. The rule stays the same. If scales are found, the fish is kosher.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi happened to come to a certain place,
they brought before him a fish
that looked like a shefarnuna,
he covered it with white vessels,
he saw scales on it, and permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel story with another way of finding scales.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fish that sheds visible scales is permitted, even if it looks like a non-kosher type.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה hears a fish dish called by a non-kosher name
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה is served a dish of small fish and hears someone call it באטי, the name of a non-kosher creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה came to אקרא דאגמא. They served him צחנתא, a dish of small fish. He heard a man calling it באטי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new story. This step only describes the situation; the next step tells what רבה בר בר חנה did about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צחנתא is a dish made from small fish. The man's choice of name, באטי, is a clue that something non-kosher might be mixed into it.

keyTerms.meaning: a dish made of small fish
name of a non-kosher sea creature

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אִיקְּלַע לְאַקְרָא דְאַגְמָא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana happened to come to Akra DeAgma,
they served him tzachanta,
he heard a certain man
who was calling it "batei."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אִיקְּלַע לְאַקְרָא דְאַגְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another fish story, but this time it ends with the food being forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: a fish dish is called by the name of a non-kosher creature.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה avoids the dish and is proven right
steps.stepSummary: He takes the name as a sign that the dish has something non-kosher in it and does not eat. In the morning he finds that it really does, and he quotes a פסוק about himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: since he calls it באטי, this shows there is something non-kosher in it. He did not eat from it. In the morning he checked it and found something non-kosher. He applied to himself the פסוק: "No sin shall befall the righteous."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה decides not to eat because of the suspicious name. The next morning he checks and finds he was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not ignore a small clue. He was careful and avoided the food until he could check it. Finding the non-kosher item proved him right, and he applied to himself the פסוק that no sin befalls a צדיק.

keyTerms.meaning: he applied a פסוק to himself

steps.whatToRemember: The fish stories show two sides: careful checking can permit a fish that looks suspicious, and a real warning sign is a reason to hold back.

phrases.english: He said: since he calls it "batei,"

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דָּבָר טָמֵא אִית בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: this shows there is something non-kosher in it,
so he did not eat from it.
In the morning he examined it,
he found something non-kosher in it,
he read about himself:
"No sin shall befall the righteous."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story set up in step 19 and closes the series of fish stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suspicious name for a dish was enough reason to avoid it, and checking showed it really was non-kosher.

steps.title: Why is a sliver of חילתית forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of a sliver of חילתית and asks why it may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "and a sliver of חילתית" may not be eaten. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of foods bought from non-Jews and asks why a piece of חילתית, a sharp spice, is forbidden to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חילתית is a plant product, so it is not non-kosher in itself. The question is what makes it forbidden when it comes from a non-Jew.

phrases.english: "And a sliver of chiltit."
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the fish stories and returns to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a sliver of חילתית from a non-Jew is forbidden to eat.

steps.title: Because non-Jews cut it with a knife
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that it is cut with a knife, and the knife probably has non-kosher fat on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they cut it with a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the problem is not the spice itself but the knife used to cut it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew's knife is assumed to have non-kosher grease on it. When the חילתית is cut, some of that fat gets into it.

phrases.english: Because they cut it with a knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The non-Jew's knife, which has non-kosher fat on it, is used to cut the חילתית.

steps.title: But a taste that spoils the food is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a difficulty: there is a known rule that a forbidden taste which makes food worse is permitted. Old fat on a knife should spoil the taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the Master said: something that gives a bad taste is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a rule that seems to argue against the answer. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the leftover fat on a knife is stale and makes food taste worse. That is נותן טעם לפגם, which is permitted. So why should the knife make the חילתית forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: gives a bad taste; a forbidden taste that spoils the food

phrases.english: Even though the Master said:
something that gives a bad taste is permitted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible problem with the answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the knife's fat makes the חילתית forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stale fat on a knife spoils the taste, and a spoiling taste is permitted, so the חילתית should be allowed.

steps.title: The sharp spice makes the fat taste good
steps.stepSummary: The sharpness of the חילתית improves the taste of the fat. So it counts as a taste that makes the food better, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sharpness of the חילתית, the fat becomes tasty. So it is like something that gives a good taste, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty. In this case the fat does not spoil the food, because the strong spice makes it taste good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of נותן טעם לפגם only works when the forbidden taste really makes the food worse. The sharpness of חילתית improves the fat, so here it is נותן טעם לשבח, and the regular rule of a forbidden taste applies.

keyTerms.meaning: gives a good taste; a forbidden taste that improves the food

steps.whatToRemember: A sliver of חילתית from a non-Jew is forbidden because the knife's fat, made tasty by the sharp spice, counts as נותן טעם לשבח and not לפגם.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the rule of נותן טעם לפגם is wrong. It is saying that rule does not fit here, because in this case the taste is good, not bad.

phrases.english: because of the sharpness of the chiltit,
the fat becomes sweet (tasty),

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם לְשֶׁבַח, וְאָסוּר.
phrases.english: so it is like something that gives a good taste, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the general rule stays, but this case does not fit it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The knife's stale fat spoils the taste, so the חילתית should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sharp spice makes the fat tasty, so it is נותן טעם לשבח and forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that נותן טעם לפגם depends on the actual effect on the food. A sharp food cut with a non-kosher knife is treated more strictly.

steps.title: Can we still buy חילתית from רבי לוי's slave?
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי's slave sold חילתית. After רבי לוי died, people asked רבי יוחנן whether they could still buy from the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי's slave used to sell חילתית. When רבי לוי passed away, people came to רבי יוחנן and asked: may we buy from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a question. Now that his master has died, can people still trust רבי לוי's slave when they buy חילתית from him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that חילתית is a problem because the knife that cuts it may carry non-kosher fat. While רבי לוי was alive, people trusted his slave. The question is whether that trust ended when רבי לוי died.

keyTerms.meaning: he passed away (literally, his soul rested)

phrases.english: The slave of רבי לוי
used to sell חילתית.
When רבי לוי passed away,
they came before רבי יוחנן
and said to him: May we buy from him?
phrases.notes: "Him" means the slave. They want to know if they can still buy חילתית from him now that his master is gone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the חילתית concern from steps 22-24 to a real case of buying from a trusted person's slave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the slave of a חבר keep his trusted status after his master dies?

steps.title: A חבר's slave is like a חבר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the slave of a חבר is treated like a חבר, so they may buy from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The slave of a חבר is like a חבר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. The slave is trusted just like his master was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבר is someone known for carefully keeping the laws. רבי יוחנן says the slave took on that same standard by living in a חבר's home, so he may be trusted. The trust belongs to the slave himself, so it continues even after the master dies.

keyTerms.meaning: a person known for carefully keeping the laws

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר הֲרֵי הוּא כְּחָבֵר.
phrases.english: The slave of a חבר is like a חבר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר הֲרֵי הוּא כְּחָבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The slave of a חבר is trusted like a חבר, so it is permitted to buy חילתית from him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עבדו של חבר הרי הוא כחבר.

steps.title: רב הונא בר מניומי buys תכלת and רב יוסף has no answer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מניומי bought תכלת from the household of רב עמרם חסידא. He asked רב יוסף whether he could rely on it, but רב יוסף did not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מניומי bought תכלת from the household of רב עמרם the pious. He came before רב יוסף, but רב יוסף did not have the answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second story about trusting a חבר's household. This step sets up a question that stays open until the next steps answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תכלת can easily be faked, so a person may only buy it from someone reliable. Here the seller was not רב עמרם himself but someone in his home. The open question is whether that person is trusted like רב עמרם.

keyTerms.meaning: תכלת, the blue dye used for ציצית
the people of his household (here, his wife)
he did not have it (the answer)

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי זְבֵן תְּכֵילְתָּא
phrases.english: רב הונא בר מניומי bought תכלת
from the people of the household of רב עמרם the pious.
He came before רב יוסף,
and it was not in his hand.
phrases.notes: In other words, רב יוסף did not know the answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי זְבֵן תְּכֵילְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a חבר's slave to a parallel case of a חבר's household, the wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up an open question: can one trust תכלת bought from a חבר's wife?

steps.title: חנן the tailor had the same experience
steps.stepSummary: חנן the tailor tells רב הונא that רב יוסף could not have known. He had faced the same question himself, and רב מתנא did not know either.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנן the tailor met him and said: How would poor יוסף know? This happened to me. I bought תכלת from the household of רבנאה, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא. I came before רב מתנא, and he did not have the answer.
steps.whatsHappening: A new character tells his own story about the very same question. This step leads up to the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנן explains that this ruling was not widely known, since two great scholars could not answer it. That prepares us to value the rare tradition from שמואל that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident, a story that happened
from where would he know it?

phrases.english: חנן the tailor met him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יוֹסֵף עַנְיָא מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and said to him: Poor יוסף, how would he know?
This incident happened to me myself:
I bought תכלת from the people of the household

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבְנָאָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: of רבנאה, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב מַתְנָא, לָא הֲוָה בִּידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and I came before רב מתנא, and he did not have the answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the open question of step 27 through a parallel story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question of trusting a חבר's wife was not commonly known.

steps.title: שמואל: a חבר's wife is like a חבר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה from הגרוניא tells חנן that שמואל ruled a חבר's wife is like a חבר, so the תכלת may be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: I came before רב יהודה of הגרוניא. He said to me: You have fallen into the right hand. This is what שמואל said: The wife of a חבר is like a חבר.
steps.whatsHappening: Finally someone knows the answer. רב יהודה quotes שמואל that a חבר's wife is trusted like a חבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question left open in steps 27-28. It matches רבי יוחנן's rule about the slave in step 26. People in a חבר's home share his trusted status.

keyTerms.meaning: you have fallen into the right hands

phrases.english: I came before רב יהודה of הגרוניא,
and he said to me: You have fallen into the right hand.
This is what שמואל said:
The wife of a חבר is like a חבר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר הֲרֵי הִיא כְּחָבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question left open in steps 27-28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חבר's wife is trusted like a חבר, so the תכלת bought from her may be relied on.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches both rules and more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא already teaches that a חבר's wife and slave are like a חבר. It adds that a dead חבר's family keeps its trusted status, and so does a courtyard that sells תכלת, until there is reason for suspicion.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned what the Rabbis taught: The wife of a חבר is like a חבר. The slave of a חבר is like a חבר. When a חבר dies, his wife, children and household keep their trusted status until they come under suspicion. Likewise, a courtyard where תכלת is sold keeps its trusted status until it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that states the same rules taught by רבי יוחנן and שמואל. This confirms both stories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא backs up both rulings. It also adds that a person or place keeps its trusted status after the חבר dies, until there is real reason for suspicion. That fits the first story, where the slave was still trusted after רבי לוי's death.
steps.whatToRemember: The people in a חבר's home, his wife, slave, children and household, are trusted like him, even after he dies. That trust lasts until they give a real reason for suspicion. A known תכלת shop keeps its trusted status the same way.
steps.confusionAlert: Trust does not end when the חבר dies. It lasts until there is a real reason for suspicion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a lasting rule: once a person or place is established as reliable, that status continues until it is actually damaged.

phrases.english: We have learned this, as the Rabbis taught:
The wife of a חבר is like a חבר;

phrases.aramaic: עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר הֲרֵי הוּא כְּחָבֵר,
phrases.english: the slave of a חבר is like a חבר;
a חבר who died:
his wife, his children, and the members of his household
remain in their trusted status until they become suspected.
And likewise, a courtyard in which they sell תכלת
remains in its trusted status
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, which talks about the courtyard ("it").

phrases.english: until it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rulings of steps 26 and 29 with a ברייתא and extends them.
steps.raayaObject: The rulings that a חבר's slave (רבי יוחנן) and wife (שמואל) are like a חבר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating both rules, plus a rule that trusted status continues after the חבר's death, and for a תכלת courtyard, until there is reason for suspicion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חבר's household is trusted like him and stays trusted until it is suspected. A place known for selling תכלת stays trusted until it is disqualified.

steps.title: Moving into or out of a חבר's household
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that people joining a חבר's household must accept חבר commitments, while people leaving a חבר's household for an עם הארץ's do not need to accept them again. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If the wife of an עם הארץ later marries a חבר, or the daughter of an עם הארץ marries a חבר, or the slave of an עם הארץ is sold to a חבר, all of them must accept the commitments of a חבר. But if the wife of a חבר later marries an עם הארץ, or the daughter of a חבר marries an עם הארץ, or the slave of a חבר is sold to an עם הארץ, they do not need to accept the commitments of a חבר from the start. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the topic of how a חבר's wife and slave are treated by bringing a ברייתא. This ברייתא deals with people who move from one kind of household to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on which way the person moves. Someone coming from an עם הארץ's home has never taken on the חבר commitments, so they must accept them now. Someone leaving a חבר's home already lived by those rules, so according to רבי מאיר they keep that status and do not need to begin again.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is not careful about details such as tithes and purity
A person who has formally committed to keep tithes and purity carefully
The commitments a person accepts when becoming a חבר
From the start; here, accepting the commitments over again

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. Moving into a חבר's home requires accepting the commitments. Moving out of a חבר's home does not, according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The wife of a non-careful person (am ha'aretz) who married a chaver,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר,
phrases.english: and likewise the daughter of an am ha'aretz who married a chaver,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לְחָבֵר —
phrases.english: and likewise the slave of an am ha'aretz who was sold to a chaver —
all of them must accept the commitments of a chaver,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: but the wife of a chaver who married an am ha'aretz,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: and likewise the daughter of a chaver who married an am ha'aretz,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ —
phrases.english: and likewise the slave of a chaver who was sold to an am ha'aretz —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵרוּת לְכַתְּחִלָּה,
phrases.english: they do not need to accept the commitments of a chaver from the start,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that a חבר's wife and slave are like a חבר, and asks what happens when they move to another household.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those entering a חבר's household must accept חבר commitments. Those leaving it for an עם הארץ's household do not need to accept them again (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: רבי יהודה says even those leaving must accept again
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר. He holds that people leaving a חבר's home for an עם הארץ's home must also accept the חבר commitments over again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They too must accept the commitments of a חבר from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the second half of רבי מאיר's ruling. In his view, even people coming from a חבר's household need to accept the commitments again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר assumes that their earlier status stays with them. רבי יהודה holds that once they live in an עם הארץ's household, that earlier trust is no longer enough, so they must accept the commitments anew.

keyTerms.meaning: They too; the people in the second group

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
they too must accept
phrases.notes: "They" means the second group: the wife, daughter or slave who left a חבר's home.

phrases.english: the commitments of a chaver from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הֵן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵרוּת לְכַתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רבי מאיר's ruling in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even those leaving a חבר's household for an עם הארץ's must newly accept חבר commitments.

steps.title: A story of a woman who changed with her husband
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר supports רבי יהודה with a story. A woman married to a חבר tied his תפילין for him, and when she later married a tax collector she tied his tax-collector's knots for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would say: There was a story with a woman who married a חבר, and she used to tie his תפילין on his arm for him. Then she married a tax collector, and she used to tie the tax collector's knots on his arm for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר brings a real-life story to support רבי יהודה. It shows that a person can change completely to match a new household.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same woman who helped her first husband with a מצוה later helped her second husband with the tools of a suspicious trade. This shows that her earlier time in a חבר's home did not guarantee anything afterward. So it makes sense to require her to accept the commitments again, as רבי יהודה says.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought as an example
תפילין, worn on the arm and head
A tax collector, often suspected of dishonesty
The knots or seals a tax collector wore as part of his job

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says someone leaving a חבר's home keeps their trusted status. רבי יהודה, backed by רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's story, says a new household can change a person, so they must accept the commitments again.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And so Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would say:
There was an incident with a certain woman who married a chaver,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה קוֹשֶׁרֶת לוֹ תְּפִילִּין עַל יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: and she used to tie tefillin on his arm for him;
she then married a tax collector,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה קוֹשֶׁרֶת לוֹ קִשְׁרֵי מוֹכֵס עַל יָדוֹ.

steps.title: רב's rule about items left with a non-Jew under one seal
steps.stepSummary: רב gives two memory codes. Items in חבי"ת are forbidden if left with a non-Jew under only one seal, and items in חמפ"ג are permitted. The גמרא begins spelling out חבי"ת: milk, meat, wine and תכלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: חבי"ת is forbidden with one seal. חמפ"ג is permitted with one seal. חבי"ת stands for חלב (milk), בשר (meat), יין (wine) and תכלת (blue dye).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. רב gives a rule about food and other items left with a non-Jew, and the גמרא begins explaining his memory codes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how much sealing is needed so that we can be sure the non-Jew did not swap or tamper with the item. For חבי"ת items, one seal is not enough. For חמפ"ג items, one seal is enough. Here the גמרא spells out only חבי"ת, and the explanation of חמפ"ג comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory codes made from the first letters of lists of items
The blue dye used for ציצית

steps.confusionAlert: חבי"ת and חמפ"ג are not words. Each one is made from the first letters of a list of items, so the code helps you remember which items are forbidden and which are permitted.

phrases.english: Rav said:
"ChBYT" is forbidden with one seal,
phrases.notes: This means items left with a non-Jew that were closed with only one seal.

phrases.english: "ChMPG" is permitted with one seal.
Milk, meat, wine, blue dye (tekhelet).

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Milk, meat, wine and תכלת left with a non-Jew under only one seal are forbidden. The items coded חמפ"ג are permitted with one seal.
